answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying identity to a slashed bond. To join, an agent locks collateral in a time-locked contract. A sybil attacker wanting a thousand fake personas cannot reuse one stake; he must lock a thousand deposits, so his budget is sliced too thin to clear reputation thresholds, and any persona caught echoing duplicate work is slashed. Forgery becomes a guaranteed loss, not a lottery ticket. The bond is no velvet cushion; it sits as inert as quartz, and the ledger re-checks each identity when it tries to dock, so every jetty of entry costs the attacker again.
